name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped spots with gray or white centers and brown borders on leaves. Nodes turn black and break easily. Neck rot causes panicles to fall over.
treatment: Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g/liter of water.
Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilizer application.
Maintain proper field sanitation and remove weed hosts.
prevention: Use resistant seed varieties like Swarna, IR64. Treat seeds with Carbendazim before sowing. Space plants properly to ensure air circulation.

name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
symptoms: Linear yellow to straw-colored stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, progressing downwards. Milky ooze droplets on leaves in humid mornings.
treatment: Spray Streptocycline at 0.1 g/liter mixed with Copper Oxychloride at 2 g/liter.
Drain excess water from the fields immediately.
Avoid spraying chemical fertilizers during early mornings.
prevention: Select healthy seeds. Treat seeds with hot water (52-54°C) for 10 minutes. Avoid nitrogen over-application.

name: Brown/Leaf Rust
symptoms: Small, oval, orange-brown pustules scattered randomly on the upper leaf surface. Pustules turn black as the crop matures.
treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC at 1 ml/liter of water.
Eradicate weed hosts like wild barberry in the vicinity.
Apply balanced NPK fertilizers to boost crop immunity.
prevention: Sow rust-resistant varieties such as HD2967, DBW187. Ensure early sowing to escape peak rust infection periods.

name: Loose Smut
symptoms: Healthy grains are replaced by black, powdery spore masses inside the wheat head. Infected heads emerge earlier than healthy ones.
treatment: Seed treatment with Carboxin (Vitavax) at 2 g/kg of seed.
Uproot and burn infected heads wrapped in a bag to prevent spore spread.
Solar seed treatment (soaking seeds in water for 4 hours, then drying in hot sun).
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Practice crop rotation with non-host crops.

name: Early Blight
symptoms: Dark spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) starting on older lower leaves. Leaves turn yellow and drop off.
treatment: Spray Mancozeb at 2 g/liter or Chlorothalonil at 2 g/liter.
Prune lower leaves up to 12 inches off the ground to improve ventilation.
Mulch soil around plants to prevent fungal spores splashing from soil.
prevention: Rotate crops every 3 years. Avoid overhead irrigation (use drip lines). Maintain proper spacing.

name: Late Blight
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown/purple. White downy growth on leaf undersides in humid weather. Dark lesions on stems.
treatment: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2 g/liter.
Destroy and burn heavily infected plant residues immediately.
Avoid high humidity microclimates by proper pruning.
prevention: Ensure good drainage. Use certified blight-resistant seeds. Apply defensive copper fungicides prior to rainy spells.

name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus
symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaf margins, thickening of leaf veins, and cup-like leaf-like structures (enations) under the leaf.
treatment: Control the whitefly vector using Imidacloprid 17.8 SL at 0.3 ml/liter.
Remove and destroy infected plants at early stages of crop growth.
Eliminate weed hosts like Sida acuta and Abutilon in and around the field.
prevention: Sow resistant Bt cotton hybrids. Avoid cotton-on-cotton continuous cultivation.

name: Common Rust
symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules appearing on both upper and lower leaf surfaces. Coalescing pustules cause leaf yellowing and death.
treatment: Spray Mancozeb at 2 g/liter if infestation is high.
Apply balanced nitrogen and potassium to support plant resilience.
Harvest early if disease spreads rapidly near maturity.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant maize cultivars. Rotate with soy or legumes. Plow under crop debris after harvesting.

name: Red Rot
symptoms: Leaves dry up starting from margins. Splitting the stem reveals red pith with white horizontal bands and an alcoholic odor.
treatment: Drench soil with Carbendazim 50 WP at 1 g/liter.
Rogue out and destroy infected sugarcane clumps instantly.
Do not practice ratoon cropping in infected fields.
prevention: Plant healthy setts selected from disease-free nurseries. Treat setts with hot water before planting. Practice crop rotation with paddy.
